decisions.text: the values are not far from zero compared with their spread

each line its own colour, handed out top to bottom by the line ends: Sweden slot 1, France slot 2, Switzerland slot 3, Russia slot 4, South Korea slot 5, Netherlands slot 6, United States slot 7, Canada slot 8, Germany slot 9, Norway slot 10
each line labelled at its end, in the text grey, none moved
no point markers: no value is isolated and no straight run hides one
highlighted, twice as thick, in the strong shade of its hue, its label bold: Netherlands; the others keep their colours and widths
the unit phrase on the top label: “12 rank”; the top gridline starts after it
time axis on two levels: row 2 Feb. 2018
the title wraps onto two lines

findings.message: chart.type line departs from the procedure, which gives bumps (changes in rank are the point (06 DP6-1): a bumps chart)
findings.title: a bumps chart when changes in rank are the message

findings.message: the unit phrase “rank” is one word; say what is counted, which subset and per what period
findings.title: a unit phrase specific enough for one reading

findings.message: 10 lines crossing 41 times: more than five lines only if they rarely cross (about once per line) and are labelled directly; else small multiples (G1.20, D-28)
findings.title: at most about five lines, more only if they rarely cross and are labelled directly

findings.message: 9 regular colours, every series labelled directly: check that similar colours never sit side by side (G4.20)
findings.title: more than eight colours only with every series labelled directly

findings.message: #b98e2f and #dd8045 are 0.023 apart under deuteranopia (at least 0.06): readers with colour-vision deficiency may not tell them apart (every series is labelled directly) (G4.18, D-34)
findings.title: colours that must be told apart survive colour-vision deficiency

source.shows: the same ranks as a standard line chart: a guided departure (R6-7), and the lines rise where a country falls behind
